chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Abbas ibn Musa, from Isḥāq ibn 'Ammār, from Abū Sārah, who said:
I asked Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him) about it, meaning temporary marriage (al-mut'ah), so he said to me, 'It is permissible.'
And do not marry except a chaste woman.
Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says, 'And those who guard their private parts.'
So do not place your private part where you do not trust your dirham (dowry/wealth).
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on temporary marriage (Mut'ah) and what are its conditions according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirms the permissibility of *al-mut'ah* (temporary marriage) while emphasizing the necessity of marrying a chaste woman (*'ififah*), citing Surah al-Mu'minun regarding the guarding of private parts. He extends this spiritual principle into a practical legal maxim, linking the moral integrity of the spouse to the security of the financial transaction (dowry), thereby ensuring that the temporary contract is not merely a physical arrangement but a secure and dignified covenant.
